title: Calculate a derived count
summary: A selector can calculate a value from stored data.
introduction: A selector can calculate a value from stored data. Your task: Mark a record as read and check the derived count.
learningObjectives: Mark a record as read and check the derived count.
Explain the example for calculate a derived count

blocks.text: A selector can calculate a value from stored data. This avoids storing two values that must always be kept in step.
Use a React project with Zustand 5 installed. Hook examples belong in React components; vanilla examples use zustand/vanilla. These package imports require your own build tool.

blocks.code:
import {useBooks} from "./book-store.js"; export default function Unread(){const count=useBooks(state=>state.books.filter(book=>!book.read).length);return

{count} unread books

;}
blocks.title: Calculate a derived count

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: The selector filters records whose read flag is false.
Reading the filtered length derives a number instead of keeping a second manually synchronised count.

blocks.text: The component counts unread records from the real book-store export.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Keep only the source facts in state when a simple derived value is enough. Repeatedly returning a fresh object from a selector needs care.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Mark a record as read and check the derived count.
